caption:
You better believe we made the most of his free flights before he turned 2!🌴✈️

On a scale of 1-5, here’s how challenging it was to travel with Theo at different ages:

✈️ 6 months old
1/5. The easiest! It might have been the combination of an all-inclusive trip and the fact that he wasn’t walking yet. All he did was nap and eat by the beach or poolside, and he slept through the entire flight.

✈️ 8-11 months old
2/5. Still relatively fine. Theo was still taking two naps a day and wasn’t mobile yet, so aside from planning around naps, everything went ok. We were also doing baby-led weaning at this time, which I’m convinced helped develop his refined palate🤣

✈️ 1-1.5 years old
4/5. The most challenging, but also the most rewarding. At this age, Theo was very mobile (though still wobbly), so we had to keep a close eye on him. He needed constant entertainment, but he also understood his surroundings much better, making the experience more meaningful.

✈️ 2-3 years old
2/5. Forget what they say about the terrible twos and them not remembering things. At this age, they’re excited by everything! It’s like traveling with a mini version of ourselves. Theo does everything we do, eats everything we eat, and even though he’s no longer flying for free, this is 1000% the best time. Yes, the tantrums still happened occasionally - but they’d happen at home anyway. I’d take beach tantrums over at-home tantrums any day. Plus nothing beats hearing, “This is the best day.”🥹

caption:
Water youuu looking at? #lafortunawaterfall

La fortuna waterfall tips:
-go early if you want those Pinterest looking pictures because it can get busy. 
-don’t do a tour bus/tour if you can. You’re able to avoid crowds if you’re driving on your own 
-water shoes are a must if you’d like to get close to the waterfall - the rocks are slippery! 
-you can swim close to the waterfall but the current is strong! There are smaller pools of water off to the side that are calmer.
-bring: water, snacks, water shoes, waterproof bag, swimsuit, microfibre/light towel
-this is a “somewhat easy” hike, even with a toddler. It’s 500 steps down. It will only take you 15 minutes to get down to the waterfall but it can take you 30+ minutes getting back up. Take your time. Enjoy the trees, search for wildlife and stop to look at all the bugs - srsly Theo’s fav part!
